subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: Should `clawhub skill publish --source-repo/--source-commit` retain an explicitly unverified source-attribution record, or should only independently server-verified GitHub imports have any stored or visible source record?
rationale: This is a permanent trust and public-verification contract; source code cannot safely infer whether publisher attribution should be visible, and it must not silently elevate client assertions.

options.title: Expose separate unverified attribution
options.body: Persist and display publisher-declared source in a clearly non-trusted field while keeping `verify` and trusted provenance limited to server-resolved imports.

options.title: Require server verification
options.body: Design an ownership and content-verification workflow before storing CLI source as trusted provenance.

options.title: Document non-visible flags
options.body: State that these fields have no public provenance effect and deprecate or remove misleading publish options if they have no remaining operational purpose.

recommendation.title: Expose separate unverified attribution
recommendation.body: Persist and display publisher-declared source in a clearly non-trusted field while keeping `verify` and trusted provenance limited to server-resolved imports.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged GitHub-backed source-sync work provides the closest current implementation context for the verified-provenance side of this decision.
